market_sizing.target_buyer: Founder (early stage) or Quality/Regulatory Manager + Head of Operations (mid stage). Decision often involves 2-3 people due to TGA compliance stakes. CFO involved at AU$3M+ revenue.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Approx. 250-500 SMB AU brands (sponsors of AUST L listed medicines + non-listed nutraceuticals selling supplement-adjacent products). CMA reports ~16,000 industry employees. Industry forecast AU$6.3B in 2025 (Complementary Medicines Australia 2025 Snapshot). Top ~30 brands (Swisse, Blackmores, Nature's Way, Caruso's, Bioglan, Vitex, Musashi, Nutra-Life, Healtheries, Aussie Bodies, ATP Science, Switch Nutrition, etc.) hold most revenue; long tail of indie brands selling via Shopify + iHerb + Chemist Warehouse + Healthy Life. [uncertain]
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: ~5,000-8,000 indie supplement brands (massive D2C cohort). UK: ~600-1,000. NZ: ~80-150. CA: ~400-800. [uncertain]
market_sizing.typical_size: 3-25 employees, AU$500K-AU$20M annual revenue. Strong bimodal distribution: early indie at AU$200-800K, scaling brands at AU$2-10M.
market_sizing.annual_revenue_band_aud: 500K-2M most common in SMB cohort. Larger Growth/Pro tier candidates at AU$2-10M.
market_sizing.growth_trend: AU industry AU$6.3B forecast 2025 (CMA). 74% of Australians use complementary medicines. Sector growing ~5-8% YoY (CMA Snapshot). Online D2C and export channels are growth engines. Strong export pillar to China + SE Asia.

fit_and_timing.manuva_fit_score: 4 — strong fit on multi-level BOMs (formulation + capsule/tab/bottle/label), lot tracking (essential for TGA recall + ARTG compliance), allocation engine. Gap: no native COA (Certificate of Analysis) workflow, no GMP audit-pack export, no batch-record sign-off chain.
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: Lot tracking ships pre-launch (good). Xero/MYOB integration improves close rate significantly (brands at AU$1M+ are bookkeeper-led). Amazon FBA connector important for brands selling US via FBA.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Growth (AU$249) for AU$1-3M brands; Pro (AU$499) for AU$3M+ multi-channel + export brands. Starter rare — even hobby supplement brands need lot tracking from day one.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 5 — TGA ARTG listing (AUD$26-115K registration costs at the high end), GMP for manufacturing, AUST L compliance, post-market surveillance, recall capability requirements. SME Assist program exists but compliance burden is severe.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Cin7 Core AU$349-549/mo (very common at AU$1-5M brands). Unleashed NZ$319-399/mo. NetSuite AU$3-10K/mo at top end (Swisse, Blackmores). SAP B1 (mid-market). Katana minor presence. MasterControl + TrackWise for QMS-heavy brands (AU$1K+/mo). Spreadsheets at the indie bottom.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: AU$249-499 well within range. Recall scenarios drive WTP — one bad batch costs AU$50K+ in recall logistics. Compliance-adjacent tools score Pro tier.
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 4 — strong path Starter -> Growth -> Pro as brand scales + adds export channels + multi-location. Add-on potential for QMS-lite features.
economics.churn_risk: 2 — high regulatory switching cost (re-validating batch records on a new system is painful), so once integrated, low churn. Risk is failed onboarding rather than gradual churn.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$500-1,500 (high — long sales cycle, need to demonstrate compliance support, often involves trial + reference checks + procurement approval). Founder-time CAC: ~15-25 hrs per close x AU$100/hr = AU$1,500-2,500.
economics.cash_cac_affordability: 2 — supplements is one of the most cash-CAC-intensive segments. Solo founder needs to ration sales-cycle time carefully.
economics.ltv_estimate_aud: AU$400 ARPU x 42mo x 75% GM (compliance support overhead) = AU$12,600.
economics.typical_seat_count: 6-20 (ops + QA + warehouse + procurement + marketing + customer service). Per-seat MRP becomes painful — flat-pricing wedge clear.
economics.multi_channel_count: 4-6 (Shopify + Amazon + iHerb + Chemist Warehouse / pharmacy distribution + export distributors + occasional wholesale).
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 30-60% B2B (pharmacy wholesale, iHerb, export distributors). Pure D2C rare; multi-channel norm.

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — LinkedIn outbound works for ops/QA managers. Email moderate. CMA member directory provides high-quality lead list. Cold outreach requires careful credibility framing — 'I'm not a TGA expert but I built MRP software designed for compliance-heavy brands'.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 4 — 'TGA batch record checklist', 'AUST L recall readiness in 10 steps', 'Cin7 vs Manuva for supplement brands' converts. Content has high regulatory authority bar — must be accurate or it actively damages trust.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 2 — LOWEST of the Tier A segments. Supplement buyers expect insider credibility (former Blackmores ops lead, ex-Swisse QA). Solo outsider founder is a credibility disadvantage. Mitigation paths: (a) recruit a CMA advisor / fractional QA consultant to lend credibility; (b) lead with software competence, not regulatory expertise ('we handle the data — you handle the chemistry'); (c) start with the indie/early-stage cohort where insider creds matter less.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: High — 10-14 weeks per case study. Brands cautious about publicising operational details due to TGA visibility.

foot_in_door_fit.design_partner_appeal: 3 — moderate. Innovator brands (indie nootropics, gut-health, mushroom adaptogens) appreciate co-design. Established brands won't risk MVP software for compliance-critical workflows. Target only the indie/early end.
foot_in_door_fit.paid_pilot_fit: 4 — strong fit. AU$249 x 3 months paid pilot signals seriousness and aligns with how supplement brands evaluate B2B SaaS. Procurement-friendly.
foot_in_door_fit.free_trial_extension_fit: 2 — counterproductive. 'Free for 6 months' undermines credibility ('what kind of compliance-grade tool gives itself away?'). Use 14-day card-required trial only after a sales conversation, not as primary funnel.
foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Estimated 30-40% CC-required trial -> paid (above ChartMogul 31.4% — buyer is highly qualified). Paid pilot 45-55%.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Paid pilot AU$249/mo x 3 months credit-on-conversion. Founder-led + CMA member directory outbound. CRITICAL: pair with a freelance/fractional TGA consultant advisor (lend their credibility on sales calls + technical webinars). Open with the indie/early-stage cohort (AU$500K-AU$2M revenue) — they're underserved by Cin7 and tolerant of outsider founders. Build 2-3 case studies before approaching CMA-member established brands.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 2 (months 3-6) — lot tracking is the prereq (ships pre-launch) but case-study credibility from cosmetics/SPF must come first. Approaching CMA brands without 3-5 logo references is premature.

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Cin7 Core ~30-35% share at AU$1-5M brands. NetSuite ~20% at top end. Unleashed ~15%. Spreadsheets + Shopify ~15% at indie end. Katana ~5%. MasterControl/TrackWise for QMS layer (sits alongside, not instead of MRP) at heavy-compliance brands.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Cin7 gaps: post-acquisition pricing rage, weak batch record workflow, no native COA management, no TGA-aligned export pack. Unleashed: similar weaknesses + NZD billing pain. Spreadsheets: total compliance risk. Manuva closes: multi-level BOMs with versioning (formulation + capsule + bottle), lot tracking with full genealogy, allocation engine, flat AU$ pricing. Gap to close on roadmap: COA upload+linking, batch sign-off chain, GMP audit export.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: Cin7 G2 complaints: 'pricing doubled after acquisition', 'no nutraceutical-specific features'. r/Nutraceutical (small) + LinkedIn ops-lead posts: 'we run COA tracking in a separate Airtable', 'recall drill = manual hell'. CMA member surveys cite digital transformation as a top-5 concern.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Must: Shopify (have), Xero/MYOB (roadmap). Important: Amazon FBA (roadmap), iHerb seller portal (gap), Chemist Warehouse EDI (gap, hard), TGA SME Assist data export (gap). Nice: Klaviyo, ShipStation, supplement-specific COA storage (Dropbox + LIMS).

partner_channels.xero_myob_partner_channel_fit: 4 — supplement brands at AU$1M+ have external accountant + bookkeeper. ProAdvisor referrals are the strongest acquisition channel once Xero/MYOB integrations ship.
partner_channels.shopify_app_store_acquisition_fit: 3 — supplement brands browse Shopify App Store but compliance buyer also wants validation outside the store. Listing helps but isn't decisive.
partner_channels.shopify_plus_partner_potential: 3 — many AU$3M+ supplement brands are on Shopify Plus. Tech Partner program useful.
partner_channels.tpl_3pl_referral_potential: 3 — 3PLs (eStore Logistics, Australia Post, Pack & Send) handle supplement fulfilment widely. Co-sell potential moderate.
partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: CMA membership AU$2-8K/yr depending on tier [uncertain]; CMA Conference sponsor AU$5-20K [uncertain]; CMA newsletter slot AU$1-3K [uncertain]. Naturally Good Expo AU$8-20K. ASMI membership AU$5-15K.

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 6-12 paying customers in 12 months. Long sales cycle + credibility climb + paid pilot phase caps volume. Funnel: 100-150 qualified leads (CMA member outreach + content inbound) -> 25-35 pilots -> 6-12 paid.
profitability_math.realistic_12mo_mrr_contribution_aud: AU$2,200-4,800 MRR at month 12 (8-12 customers x AU$350-400 blended).
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: Sequence: (1) months 0-2: enrol 1 fractional TGA/QA advisor for credibility (equity or retainer); (2) months 3-5: land 2 indie supplement design partners (early-stage, <AU$1M revenue, founder-led, less credentialing pressure); (3) months 4-6: publish 'AUST L lot tracking checklist' + 'recall in 7 days, not 7 weeks' cornerstone content; (4) months 6-9: shift to paid pilots; CMA newsletter ad; (5) months 9-12: 4-6 paid customers, target AU$2-4K MRR contribution. This segment unlikely to hit AU$3-5K MRR floor alone — combine with ceramics + cosmetics for cumulative floor. But ARPU + LTV mean this is critical to AU$1M ARR aspirational.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~210 customers at AU$400 ARPU. In aspirational mix, this segment contributes ~80-120 customers (~AU$380-575K ARR) — likely the #1 revenue contributor if Manuva can solve the credibility climb. Highest LTV / lowest churn of any Tier A segment once landed.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 2 — heavy onboarding (20-30 hours per customer: BOM setup + lot config + COA workflow + compliance Q&A). Support load high (regulatory escalations). Solo founder caps at ~10-12 active supplement customers before quality degrades.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 4-7 months on cash CAC; 6-10 months fully loaded.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: High — compliance support burns hours. Without product investments in COA + batch-sign-off + audit export, GM erodes to ~65-70%. Roadmap investment needed to bring GM to 75-80%.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 2 — highest ARPU + LTV of Tier A, low churn once landed, defensible wedge if compliance-grade. But credibility climb and bandwidth constraints make it a Phase-2 segment, not Phase-1. Top priority for the AU$1M ARR aspirational path; not for the 12-month MRR floor.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks: (1) credibility — outsider founder hits a real wall without a TGA-credentialed advisor; (2) feature gap (COA + batch sign-off + GMP export) requires roadmap investment before Manuva can credibly claim 'compliance-ready'; (3) one botched recall scenario on a Manuva customer is existential PR risk — must over-engineer the lot tracking workflow before scaling; (4) NetSuite + MasterControl are stickier than Cin7 — focus on the AU$500K-AU$3M revenue band, not Swisse-scale. Things to verify: actual addressable count (TGA ARTG sponsor count for AUST L excluding multi-product enterprise sponsors); willingness of CMA to allow software-vendor membership tier; whether iHerb seller portal API exists.
